claim: The European Commission closed its DMA user-choice-obligations investigation against Apple on 23 April 2025 following 'constructive dialogue,' after Apple streamlined the browser choice screen, centralized default-settings management, and made Safari uninstallable — but retains ongoing monitoring authority rather than granting permanent clearance.
stance_target: whether regulatory pressure on Apple's default settings is a one-time resolved matter or an ongoing constraint
scope_conditions: EU iPhone default settings, closed 23 April 2025
quoted_support: The Commission will keep monitoring Apple's measures and continue its regulatory dialogue to ensure full and effective user choice, as safeguarded by the DMA.

claim: Simultaneously with closing the choice-screen probe, the Commission issued new preliminary findings that Apple's Core Technology Fee, eligibility requirements, and burdensome install process for alternative app stores breach the DMA, and that Apple failed to show these measures are strictly necessary and proportionate.
stance_target: Apple has fully resolved its DMA App Store distribution exposure
scope_conditions: EU alternative app store/web distribution, as of 23 April 2025
quoted_support: Developers wanting to use alternative app distribution channels on iOS are disincentivised from doing so as this requires them to opt for business terms which include a new fee (Apple's Core Technology Fee)... The Commission has preliminarily found that Apple has failed to demonstrate that the measures put in place are strictly necessary and proportionate.
